rationale: Round 0 compiled and ran correctly with no ICE, so this round raises obfuscation pressure while staying within the runtime/size envelope. SUB is weighted highest for diversity and security because it is nearly free and composes with every other pass; SPLIT is kept cheap to precondition FLA by fragmenting the 750-byte main and the loop-heavy sums/eden/next bodies. FLA is the primary control-flow protector for these small but loop-intensive functions (life's grid update loops run many iterations, so flattening's dispatcher overhead is acceptable relative to the memory-access-dominated workload). BCF is pushed up from a presumably conservative round-0 value to add opaque predicates on hot loops, but its RuntimeCost and SizeCost are capped at ~0.35-0.4 since the binary's total text is only ~2.1 KB and unbounded bogus-flow inflation would be disproportionate. IBR, ICALL, and IGV get moderately strong security/diversity weights to break static call-graph and data-flow recovery (the C++ virtual-free but class-heavy code of living/empty/eden makes indirected calls and globals effective against xref-based analysis), with CorrectnessRisk kept at ~0.2 to preserve the correct behavior already achieved, since ICALL/IGV lowering is the most fragile path for C++ name-mangled and vtable-adjacent code.
